currentContext.strengths: Five-decade delivery track record used as brand capital: the AR cites 57+ years of project delivery, over 46,000 families housed and 20+ million sq. ft. handed over.|Deliberate geographic concentration in Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru rather than dispersing across fragmented geographies, which the Company links to faster execution cycles and improved capital efficiency.|Asset-light expansion model (joint ventures, joint development agreements and MHADA/SRA/society redevelopment) that reduces capital intensity while expanding the development footprint.|Deleveraged balance sheet: debt-to-equity reduced to 0.53x, described as the healthiest in the Company's listed history, giving flexibility to align sales with market cycles rather than chase volume.|Large strategic land reserve, notably the 55-acre Kanjurmarg parcel and the Wadala master development, providing a multi-year, in-house development pipeline.|Reputation for ahead-of-schedule delivery, which the Company positions as economic capital supporting stronger bookings and superior realisations.|Marketing and CRM technology stack tracking buyers from first digital enquiry to post-booking engagement, with spend rebalanced toward performance-led channels.
currentContext.strategies: Strategy 1 - Unlock the owned land bank at Wadala and Kanjurmarg: inventory the Company already owns in micro-markets it has understood for decades, carrying no acquisition cost and no land risk, released in a phased sequence designed to maximise long-term value at every stage.|Wadala is being developed across four progressive eras - from the i-Land township, to Manhattan luxury residential, to a revised Boutique Office campus, to a planned uber-luxury residential tower - with each phase intended to raise the price ceiling for the next.|Kanjurmarg is being built out as a landmark mixed-use destination over an approximately nine-year timeline, with the next phase focused on infrastructure creation (roads and allied works) and a planned strategic tie-up on a 7-acre parcel to support land conversion, fund initial capital expenditure and establish pricing benchmarks.|Strategy 2 - Asset-light inorganic growth through Joint Ventures, Joint Development Agreements and redevelopment partnerships (MHADA-, SRA- and society-led), expanding the development footprint without a proportional balance sheet burden; stated structural advantages are lower upfront land costs, faster project turnaround and improved return on equity.|Leverage fifty-eight years of delivery and reputation as a sourcing advantage, with housing societies seeking trusted redevelopment partners increasingly approaching Ajmera first.|Strategy 3 - Maximise strategic locational advantage and diverse offerings: develop where infrastructure, connectivity and economic activity are converging, deepening presence in high-growth micro-markets rather than merely expanding footprint.|Keep Mumbai the cornerstone of growth, concentrating on Wadala, Kanjurmarg, Vikhroli, Bandra, Andheri, Juhu and Borivali, where Metro corridors, Atal Setu, the Coastal Road, Navi Mumbai International Airport and emerging business districts are reshaping accessibility and long-term development potential.|Diversify geographically into Bengaluru on the strength of its technology employment base and residential demand, and re-enter the Pune market leveraging brand, market understanding and execution capability.|Maintain a diversified product portfolio spanning premium, luxury and mid-income residential, township developments and boutique commercial assets.|Run a balanced pipeline of owned and asset-light projects to pursue growth while optimising capital allocation, supported by a disciplined execution framework aimed at speed, precision, quality and timely completion.|Sustain the '5x' trajectory: since FY21 net profit has grown 5.1x (38% CAGR), revenue 3.1x and EBITDA 3.0x while debt-to-equity fell from 1.13x to 0.53x, and management states the platform can now sustain a considerably larger scale of ambition.|Materiality-led ESG agenda organised around five themes: environmental sustainability (green building practices and certifications, energy and water efficiency, climate resilience, waste management, biodiversity), stakeholder trust and development, responsible business practices (RERA compliance, transparent governance, ethical land acquisition, sustainable supply chain), workforce well-being, and technology and cybersecurity (digital infrastructure, data privacy and cyber risk).
currentContext.expansion: The sections routed into this bundle carry no project-level capex or expansion narrative for the Company - no named project, commissioning date, capacity addition or rupee capital-expenditure quantum appears in the text provided. What the bundle does state on structure is that as at the year under review the Company had fifteen subsidiaries, one associate and two joint venture companies, and that no subsidiary, associate or joint venture company was formed or ceased to exist during the financial year, so the group footprint was unchanged in FY26. The remainder of the bundle is sector context rather than company expansion: management describes Indian real estate as moving from cyclical expansion to a more structural growth phase, sized at approximately USD 585 billion in 2026 and projected to reach nearly USD 926 billion by 2031 and contributing about 7.3% of GDP, with a FY27 budgetary allocation of Rs 85,522.39 crore to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Within that backdrop the Company points to Mumbai (capital values in key micro-markets reaching approximately Rs 27,000 per sq. ft., and redevelopment as a major growth catalyst with 229 development agreements executed in 2025 against 196 the previous year, a 16% year-on-year increase) and Bengaluru (approximately 49,252 residential unit launches in 2025, office absorption of nearly 28.7 million sq. ft., and Grade A accounting for roughly 97% of transacted office space) as the markets where its opportunity sits. Faster project approvals and alignment with Viksit Bharat @ 2047 are listed as intended outcomes of its regulatory engagement. As a real-estate developer the Company is asset-light in the manufacturing sense and discloses no installed capacity, and no named capital-expenditure disclosure block is present in this bundle.
currentContext.mdna: Management frames Indian real estate as transitioning from cyclical expansion to a more structural growth phase, supported by rapid urbanisation, rising incomes, infrastructure investment and increasing institutional participation, creating long-term opportunity across residential, commercial, retail, hospitality and industrial real estate.|The Indian real estate market is estimated at approximately USD 585 billion in 2026 and projected to reach nearly USD 926 billion by 2031, driven by strong corporate leasing, proliferation of Global Capability Centres, improving liquidity and growing REIT-led investment; the sector is put at roughly 7.3% of GDP in 2026.|Policy support is cited via a budgetary allocation of Rs 85,522.39 crore for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in FY27.|Mumbai demand is described as sustained across premium residential and mixed-use developments, with capital values in key micro-markets reaching approximately Rs 27,000 per sq. ft.|Redevelopment is identified as a major growth catalyst in Mumbai: 229 development agreements were executed in 2025 versus 196 in the prior year, a 16% year-on-year increase, with Borivali, Andheri, Bandra, Malad and Ghatkopar the leading micro-markets; cumulatively 1,094 development agreements between January 2020 and 15 March 2026 unlocked 432 acres and are expected to generate 59,000 housing units (Knight Frank India).|Bengaluru is positioned as India's leading office market and most dynamic residential market, with approximately 49,252 residential unit launches in 2025, office absorption of nearly 28.7 million sq. ft., Grade A accounting for about 97% of transacted office space, and an estimated USD 2.2 billion of real estate investment inflows in 2025 - the highest among Indian cities.|Pune fundamentals are described as resilient despite residential sales moderating from peak levels, with rising capital values, larger average transaction sizes and a shift toward premium and larger-format homes, while the commercial segment sees record leasing and is the key growth driver.|Company-level margin/return levers cited: no land acquisition cost on the owned Mumbai land bank, lower upfront land cost and faster turnaround under asset-light structures, and a leaner balance sheet that permits aligning sales with market cycles to protect margins rather than chasing volume.|Ajmera's owned Mumbai land bank carries a future development potential of 10.4 million sq. ft. across Wadala and Kanjurmarg.|Wadala represents a Rs 17,841 crore unlocking opportunity over the next four years.|Wadala Manhattan luxury residential: Phase 1 at 90% sold and Phase 2 at 48% sold.|Wadala revised Boutique Office campus of 20.1 lakh sq. ft. with GDV of Rs 7,261 crore; phase 1 launch planned Q3 FY27.|An uber-luxury residential tower is planned at Wadala.|Kanjurmarg 55-acre parcel: estimated development potential of 71.7 lakh sq. ft. (29.5 lakh sq. ft. residential and 42.2 lakh sq. ft. retail, hospitality and commercial) with estimated GDV of over Rs 22,618 crore, across a development timeline of approximately nine years.|Total owned land bank in Mumbai carries future development potential of 10.4 million sq. ft.|In FY26, five projects with a combined GDV of Rs 2,433 crore were secured.|The FY27 pipeline includes further SRA project launches, MHADA redevelopments and JD/JVA transactions.|The development pipeline spans Mumbai micro-markets including Vikhroli, Bhandup, Ghatkopar, Bandra, Borivali, Juhu and Andheri, and extends to Bengaluru, with a re-entry into Pune.

risks.risk: Regulatory and RERA compliance / approval dependency
risks.note: 'Regulatory and RERA compliance' is listed among the Company's key material themes under Responsible Business Practices, and the stakeholder framework names 'faster project approvals' and 'zero regulatory penalties' as the outcomes it seeks from engaging regulators. For a developer, approvals and RERA obligations sit directly on the critical path of project launch, completion and revenue recognition, so any slippage in clearances or a compliance breach delays cash flows.

risks.risk: Climate resilience and environmental performance of the built portfolio
risks.note: Environmental sustainability is the first key material theme, covering green building practices and certifications, energy and water efficiency, climate resilience and adaptation, waste management and recycling, and biodiversity. Investors are explicitly engaged on 'mitigation measures for climate change risks and reduction of operational carbon footprint', making both physical climate exposure at project sites and transition expectations on green building standards a structural cost and saleability risk.

risks.risk: Technology, data privacy and cyber risk
risks.note: 'Technology & Cybersecurity' is a standalone key material theme covering digital infrastructure strengthening and data privacy and cyber risk management. The Company runs customer-facing digital channels and CRM-based buyer data, so a breach or systems failure would carry both operational and customer-trust consequences.

'Ethical land acquisition and development' is called out as a material issue under Responsible Business Practices. Land title, acquisition conduct and development rights are the foundational input for a developer; a defect or dispute here is not recoverable through operating performance.

risks.risk: Supply chain reliability and contractor performance
risks.note: The stakeholder framework identifies supplier engagement outcomes as 'ensuring quality and meeting project schedules', 'reliable supply chain' and 'improved project timelines', with sustainable supply chain practices a material theme. Construction schedules and cost are therefore exposed to supplier and contractor execution, and procurement cost movement flows straight into project margins.

risks.risk: Workforce health and safety at construction sites
risks.note: 'Workforce Well-being' is a key material theme covering health and safety standards and employee engagement, and the community engagement framework names 'safe working practices near construction sites'. Site safety incidents in a construction business carry regulatory, cost and reputational consequences and can halt work at a project.

risks.risk: Reliance on brand and customer trust for sales velocity
risks.note: The customer engagement framework rests the value proposition on a legacy brand, superior living experience and quality homes, with outcomes framed as enhanced customer trust and repeat purchases contributing to sales growth. Customer satisfaction and experience is a named material theme, so a delivery or quality failure would erode the reputational asset the sales model depends on.

risks.risk: Financial risk, leverage and compliance control effectiveness
risks.note: CRISIL Ratings assigned a corporate credit rating of CRISIL A-/Stable and re-affirmed a CRISIL A-/Stable long-term bank loan rating on a Rs 500 crore scale, so funding cost and access are rating-linked. The Board notes a comprehensive Risk Management Policy, a Risk Management Committee constituted under Regulation 21 of the SEBI Listing Regulations and Audit Committee oversight of financial risks and controls; against that, the year did see a lapse in timely registration of charges created in favour of Mercedes-Benz Financial Services India Private Limited and Tata Capital Housing Finance Limited, attributed to delayed receipt of documents from those institutions - a filing-discipline point even though no auditor reported fraud and no material regulatory, court or tribunal order was passed during the year.

one-line thesis: Ajmera delivered record presales of INR1,701cr (57% YoY) and PAT of INR157cr (24% YoY) driven by luxury launches and disciplined execution, while strategically normalizing debt-to-equity from 0.53x to 1.00x guidance to fund INR19,518cr pipeline; the shift from pure growth to calibrated leverage signals maturity and unlocks high-value redevelopment potential in Wadala, Versova, and Kanjurmarg.

guidance: revenue growth: 50%+ YoY implied from INR10,432cr visibility; margin: sustained at ~28% EBITDA margin; order inflow: INR1,800cr targeted for FY27; capex/commissioning: INR6,324cr launch pipeline (FY27), Kanjurmarg redevelopment to commence post-regulatory clearance (H2FY27)
order book & pipeline: INR4,108cr total visibility (INR1,837cr committed sales + INR2,270cr unsold inventory); INR6,324cr upcoming launch pipeline; total revenue visibility INR10,432cr
segment / subsidiary detail: Luxury Residential: Manhattan 1 (90% sold, AR INR37k/sqft), Manhattan 2 (48% sold, AR INR35k/sqft), Vann Versova (launched Q4, avg 1,700 sqft, 4BR focus); Commercial: 33Fifteen Bandra (17% sold), Boutique Offices (Q3FY27 launch); Redevelopment: Greenfinity (94% sold), Vihara Bhandup (81% sold), Iris & Marina Bengaluru (88%, 69% sold); Asset-light BD: INR2,433cr secured across 5 projects; Kanjurmarg (11-acre, INR13,194cr GDV) pending land conversion
growth verticals / optionality: Kanjurmarg redevelopment (INR13,194cr GDV) with residential, commercial, retail mix; Versova entry validates premium micro-market expansion; asset-light BD pipeline targeting INR1,800cr in FY27; potential SPV-level equity partnerships to unlock land value without diluting parent balance sheet
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin sustained at ~28% despite cost inflation; pricing power evident: Manhattan AR up 10-15% YoY; premium positioning (township amenities) offsets land/construction cost pressures; no margin compression observed
capex / expansion: INR64cr PPE (up from INR35cr) due to capitalization of Mivan sliding systems across projects; no explicit FY27 capex figure given, but launch pipeline of INR6,324cr implies significant development spend; Kanjurmarg pre-construction activities (police housing, master planning) already underway
capital allocation: Debt reduction priority achieved (D/E 0.53x); FY27 guidance shifts to 1.00x to fund launches and Kanjurmarg; SPV-level equity partnerships planned for Kanjurmarg to avoid parent-level dilution; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on internal cash generation (INR3,150cr pretax cash flow visibility from OC projects)
risks & watch-items: Regulatory delays in Kanjurmarg land conversion; geopolitical headwinds causing 10-20 day delays in buyer decisions; competition from Raymond in Wadala (though Ajmera claims superior amenity-driven differentiation); potential oversupply in luxury segment if launches accelerate too rapidly
management quality / tone: Confident, calibrated, and mature; leadership emphasizes disciplined execution over aggressive growth, acknowledges geopolitical caution but sees structural demand; tone shifts from 'explosive growth' to 'sustainable scaling' with clear guidance on leverage normalization and SPV funding strategy
non-obvious takeaways: Mivan sliding systems capitalized as PPE (INR29cr increase) is a non-cash accounting benefit that improves EBITDA margin without real cost savings; Kanjurmarg SPV equity tie-ups imply valuation upside not reflected in parent market cap; Versova launch strategy (slow, steady absorption) mirrors Lokhandwala playbook — patience over velocity

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is primarily engaged in real estate development, building residential and commercial projects for homebuyers and occupiers in its core urban micro-markets of Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru. It states it has handed over more than 20 million square feet of residential and commercial space and housed over 46,000 families, and describes a market-differentiated portfolio built around a legacy brand, a large strategic land reserve and modern construction technology. Growth is pursued through joint ventures, joint development agreements and redevelopment routes (MHADA, SRA and society-led projects), which the Company says structurally reduces capital intensity while expanding its development footprint.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management frames Indian real estate as transitioning from cyclical expansion to a more structural growth phase, supported by rapid urbanisation, rising incomes, infrastructure investment and increasing institutional participation, creating long-term opportunity across residential, commercial, retail, hospitality and industrial real estate.
- The Indian real estate market is estimated at approximately USD 585 billion in 2026 and projected to reach nearly USD 926 billion by 2031, driven by strong corporate leasing, proliferation of Global Capability Centres, improving liquidity and growing REIT-led investment; the sector is put at roughly 7.3% of GDP in 2026.
- Policy support is cited via a budgetary allocation of Rs 85,522.39 crore for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in FY27.
- Mumbai demand is described as sustained across premium residential and mixed-use developments, with capital values in key micro-markets reaching approximately Rs 27,000 per sq. ft.
- Redevelopment is identified as a major growth catalyst in Mumbai: 229 development agreements were executed in 2025 versus 196 in the prior year, a 16% year-on-year increase, with Borivali, Andheri, Bandra, Malad and Ghatkopar the leading micro-markets; cumulatively 1,094 development agreements between January 2020 and 15 March 2026 unlocked 432 acres and are expected to generate 59,000 housing units (Knight Frank India).
- Bengaluru is positioned as India's leading office market and most dynamic residential market, with approximately 49,252 residential unit launches in 2025, office absorption of nearly 28.7 million sq. ft., Grade A accounting for about 97% of transacted office space, and an estimated USD 2.2 billion of real estate investment inflows in 2025 - the highest among Indian cities.
- Pune fundamentals are described as resilient despite residential sales moderating from peak levels, with rising capital values, larger average transaction sizes and a shift toward premium and larger-format homes, while the commercial segment sees record leasing and is the key growth driver.
- Company-level margin/return levers cited: no land acquisition cost on the owned Mumbai land bank, lower upfront land cost and faster turnaround under asset-light structures, and a leaner balance sheet that permits aligning sales with market cycles to protect margins rather than chasing volume.
- Ajmera's owned Mumbai land bank carries a future development potential of 10.4 million sq. ft. across Wadala and Kanjurmarg.
- Wadala represents a Rs 17,841 crore unlocking opportunity over the next four years.
- Wadala Manhattan luxury residential: Phase 1 at 90% sold and Phase 2 at 48% sold.
- Wadala revised Boutique Office campus of 20.1 lakh sq. ft. with GDV of Rs 7,261 crore; phase 1 launch planned Q3 FY27.
- An uber-luxury residential tower is planned at Wadala.
- Kanjurmarg 55-acre parcel: estimated development potential of 71.7 lakh sq. ft. (29.5 lakh sq. ft. residential and 42.2 lakh sq. ft. retail, hospitality and commercial) with estimated GDV of over Rs 22,618 crore, across a development timeline of approximately nine years.
- Total owned land bank in Mumbai carries future development potential of 10.4 million sq. ft.
- In FY26, five projects with a combined GDV of Rs 2,433 crore were secured.
- The FY27 pipeline includes further SRA project launches, MHADA redevelopments and JD/JVA transactions.
- The development pipeline spans Mumbai micro-markets including Vikhroli, Bhandup, Ghatkopar, Bandra, Borivali, Juhu and Andheri, and extends to Bengaluru, with a re-entry into Pune.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin sustained at ~28% despite cost inflation; pricing power evident: Manhattan AR up 10-15% YoY; premium positioning (township amenities) offsets land/construction cost pressures; no margin compression observed

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt reduction priority achieved (D/E 0.53x); FY27 guidance shifts to 1.00x to fund launches and Kanjurmarg; SPV-level equity partnerships planned for Kanjurmarg to avoid parent-level dilution; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on internal cash generation (INR3,150cr pretax cash flow visibility from OC projects)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The sections routed into this bundle carry no project-level capex or expansion narrative for the Company - no named project, commissioning date, capacity addition or rupee capital-expenditure quantum appears in the text provided. What the bundle does state on structure is that as at the year under review the Company had fifteen subsidiaries, one associate and two joint venture companies, and that no subsidiary, associate or joint venture company was formed or ceased to exist during the financial year, so the group footprint was unchanged in FY26. The remainder of the bundle is sector context rather than company expansion: management describes Indian real estate as moving from cyclical expansion to a more structural growth phase, sized at approximately USD 585 billion in 2026 and projected to reach nearly USD 926 billion by 2031 and contributing about 7.3% of GDP, with a FY27 budgetary allocation of Rs 85,522.39 crore to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Within that backdrop the Company points to Mumbai (capital values in key micro-markets reaching approximately Rs 27,000 per sq. ft., and redevelopment as a major growth catalyst with 229 development agreements executed in 2025 against 196 the previous year, a 16% year-on-year increase) and Bengaluru (approximately 49,252 residential unit launches in 2025, office absorption of nearly 28.7 million sq. ft., and Grade A accounting for roughly 97% of transacted office space) as the markets where its opportunity sits. Faster project approvals and alignment with Viksit Bharat @ 2047 are listed as intended outcomes of its regulatory engagement. As a real-estate developer the Company is asset-light in the manufacturing sense and discloses no installed capacity, and no named capital-expenditure disclosure block is present in this bundle.

management_tone.body: Confident, calibrated, and mature; leadership emphasizes disciplined execution over aggressive growth, acknowledges geopolitical caution but sees structural demand; tone shifts from 'explosive growth' to 'sustainable scaling' with clear guidance on leverage normalization and SPV funding strategy

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Five-decade delivery track record used as brand capital: the AR cites 57+ years of project delivery, over 46,000 families housed and 20+ million sq. ft. handed over.
- Deliberate geographic concentration in Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru rather than dispersing across fragmented geographies, which the Company links to faster execution cycles and improved capital efficiency.
- Asset-light expansion model (joint ventures, joint development agreements and MHADA/SRA/society redevelopment) that reduces capital intensity while expanding the development footprint.
- Deleveraged balance sheet: debt-to-equity reduced to 0.53x, described as the healthiest in the Company's listed history, giving flexibility to align sales with market cycles rather than chase volume.
- Large strategic land reserve, notably the 55-acre Kanjurmarg parcel and the Wadala master development, providing a multi-year, in-house development pipeline.
- Reputation for ahead-of-schedule delivery, which the Company positions as economic capital supporting stronger bookings and superior realisations.
- Marketing and CRM technology stack tracking buyers from first digital enquiry to post-booking engagement, with spend rebalanced toward performance-led channels.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory delays in Kanjurmarg land conversion; geopolitical headwinds causing 10-20 day delays in buyer decisions; competition from Raymond in Wadala (though Ajmera claims superior amenity-driven differentiation); potential oversupply in luxury segment if launches accelerate too rapidly

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Mivan sliding systems capitalized as PPE (INR29cr increase) is a non-cash accounting benefit that improves EBITDA margin without real cost savings; Kanjurmarg SPV equity tie-ups imply valuation upside not reflected in parent market cap; Versova launch strategy (slow, steady absorption) mirrors Lokhandwala playbook — patience over velocity

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strategy 1 - Unlock the owned land bank at Wadala and Kanjurmarg: inventory the Company already owns in micro-markets it has understood for decades, carrying no acquisition cost and no land risk, released in a phased sequence designed to maximise long-term value at every stage.
- Wadala is being developed across four progressive eras - from the i-Land township, to Manhattan luxury residential, to a revised Boutique Office campus, to a planned uber-luxury residential tower - with each phase intended to raise the price ceiling for the next.
- Kanjurmarg is being built out as a landmark mixed-use …
